source_text: Ita cum prudentibus parum licet, vilibus autem quod libet etiam licet seditionum decreto exclusa est de Ecclesiis censura virtutum; nobisque hoc apud homines vulgi officit, quod accessio erroris esse renuimus; vulgi, inquam, qui sententiae meritum de prosperitatibus ponderans, eam veriorem aestimat quam pluribus placere conspexerit.
pass_a_gloss: Thus, when little is allowed to the prudent, but to the cheap even whatever they please is allowed, the censure of virtues has been shut out from the Churches by a decree of seditions; and this hurts us among the people of the crowd, that we refuse to be an addition of error; of the crowd, I say, which, weighing the desert of a sentence from prosperities, estimates that one truer which it has seen to please more people.

lemmas.lexica: LS meritum=desert; Blaise without later merit-system

pass_b_english: Thus, when the wise are allowed little while the worthless are allowed whatever they please, the judgment of virtue has been expelled from the churches by the decree of rioters. What counts against us among the common people is our refusal to swell the ranks of error. I mean the crowd that weighs the worth of an opinion by its success and judges it truer the more people it sees approving it.

choices.why: Glossary: avoid modern merit-theology; Julian means deserved outcome.
Cardinal-virtue context (Stoic four); not 'power' unless the sentence is about force.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
